source_text: Nobis inferi non nuda cavositas, nec subdivalis aliqua mundi sentina creduntur: sed in fossa terrae, et in alio vastitas, et in ipsis visceribus ejus abstrusa profunditas. Siquidem Christum in corde terrae triduum mortis legimus expunctum, id est in recessu intimo et interno et in ipsa terra operto, et intra ipsam clauso, et inferioribus adhuc abyssis superstructo. Quod si Christus Deus, quia et homo, mortuus secundum Scripturas, et sepultus secundum easdem, hic quoque legi satisfecit, forma humanae mortis apud inferos functus; nec ante ascendit in sublimiora coelorum, quam descendit in inferiora terrarum, ut illic Patriarchas et Prophetas compotes sui faceret, habes et regionem inferum subterraneam credere, et illos cubito pellere, qui satis superbe non putant animas fidelium inferis dignas, servi super dominum, et discipuli super magistrum, aspernati, si forte, in Abrahae sinu exspectandae resurrectionis solatium carpere. «Sed in hoc, inquiunt, Christus inferos adiit, ne nos adiremus: caeterum, quod discrimen ethnicorum et Christianorum, si carcer mortuis idem?» Quo ergo anima modo exhalabit in coelum, Christo illic adhuc sedente ad dexteram Patris, nondum Dei jussu per tubam archangeli audito, nondum illis quos Domini adventus in saeculo invenerit obviam ei creptis in aerem, cum his qui mortui in Christo primi resurgent? Nulli patet coelum, terra adhuc salva, ne dixerim clausa. Cum transactione enim mundi reserabuntur regna coelorum. Sed in aethere dormitio nostra, cum pueris Platonis; aut in aere, cum Ario; aut circa lunam, cum Endymionibus Stoicorum: «Imo, inquis, in paradiso, quo jam tunc et Patriarchae et Prophetae appendices Dominicae resurrectionis, ab inferis migraverint.» Et, quomodo Joanni in spiritu paradisi regio revelata, quae subjicitur altari, nullas alias animas apud se praeter martyrum ostendit? Quomodo Perpetua fortissima martyr, sub die passionis, in revelatione paradisi, solos illic commartyres suos vidit, nisi quia nullis romphaea paradisi janitrix cedit, nisi qui in Christo decesserint, non in Adam? Nova mors pro Deo, et extraordinaria pro Christo, alio et privato excipitur hospitio. Agnosce itaque differentiam ethnici et fidelis in morte. Si pro Deo occumbas, ut Paracletus monet, non in mollibus febribus et in lectulis, sed in martyriis, si crucem tuam tollas, et sequaris Dominum, ut ipse praecepit; tota paradisi clavus tuus sanguis est. Habes etiam de Paradiso a nobis libellum, quo constituimus omnem animam apud inferos sequestrari in diem Domini.
pass_a_gloss: To us, the underworld is not believed to be a mere empty cavity, nor some kind of sewer of the world, but in the pit of the earth, and in another vastness, and in the very bowels of it, a hidden depth. For we read that Christ, in the heart of the earth, was spent, that is, in the innermost and internal recess, and in the earth itself covered, and within it enclosed, and with the lower abysses still built over. But if Christ, God because also man, died according to the Scriptures, and was buried according to the same, here too He satisfied the law, having undergone the form of human death among the dead; nor did He ascend into the higher heavens before He descended into the lower earth, so that there He might make the Patriarchs and Prophets partakers of Himself. You have, therefore, to believe in the subterranean region of the underworld, and to reject those who haughtily think that the souls of the faithful are not worthy of the underworld, servants above their Lord, and disciples above their Master, despised, if perhaps, to pluck the comfort of the resurrection to be awaited in Abraham's bosom. But they say, 'In this, Christ went to the underworld, so that we might not go: but what difference is there between pagans and Christians, if the prison of the dead is the same?' Therefore, in what way will the soul breathe out into heaven, with Christ still sitting at the right hand of the Father, not yet having heard the command of God through the trumpet of the archangel, not yet having met those whom the coming of the Lord found in the world, creeping into the air with those who, having died in Christ, will be the first to rise? Heaven is not open to anyone, the earth still being safe, or rather, I should say, closed. For with the transaction of the world, the kingdoms of heaven will be opened. But our rest is in the ether, with the children of Plato; or in the air, with Arius; or around the moon, with the Stoics of Endymion: 'Indeed,' you say, 'in paradise, to which already then the Patriarchs and Prophets, appendages of the Lord's resurrection, had migrated from the underworld.' And how did John, in the spirit, reveal the region of paradise, which is subject to the altar, show no other souls with him except those of the martyrs? How did Perpetua, the strongest martyr, on the day of her passion, in the revelation of paradise, see only her fellow martyrs there, unless because the doorkeeper of paradise yields to no one, except those who have died in Christ, not in Adam? A new death for God, and an extraordinary one for Christ, is received in another and private hospitality. Recognize, therefore, the difference between the pagan and the faithful in death. If you die for God, as the Paraclete advises, not in soft fevers and in beds, but in martyrdoms, if you take up your cross and follow the Lord, as He Himself commanded; all of paradise is yours, your blood is the key. You also have from us a booklet about Paradise, in which we establish that every soul is separated among the dead until the day of the Lord.
pass_b_english: We do not imagine the underworld as a mere hollow cavity or some cosmic sewer; we locate it in the pit of the earth, in a second vastness, a hidden depth buried in the planet's very bowels. Scripture says Christ spent three days of death in the heart of the earth (Matt 12:40) — that is, in its innermost, internal recess, covered over with earth, shut inside it, with the lower abysses still roofed above him. Since Christ, God because he is also man, died according to the Scriptures and was buried according to them (1 Cor 15:3-4), he here too satisfied the law by undergoing the form of human death among the dead; he did not ascend into the higher heavens before he descended into the lower parts of the earth (Eph 4:9), so that there he might make the Patriarchs and Prophets partakers of himself. You must therefore believe in a subterranean underworld region, and shove aside those who haughtily decide that the souls of the faithful are unworthy of the underworld — servants above their Lord, disciples above their Master — despising, if they can, the comfort of the resurrection waiting in Abraham's bosom (Luke 16:22).

They object, 'Christ went to the underworld in this very way so that we would not have to; but what difference remains between pagans and Christians if the dead share the same prison?' Very well: how exactly will a soul breathe its last into heaven while Christ is still seated at the Father's right hand (Ps 110:1; Heb 1:3), before God's command has been heard through the archangel's trumpet (1 Thess 4:16), before those whom the Lord's coming finds alive in the world have been caught up into the air together with the dead in Christ who rise first (1 Thess 4:17)? Heaven is open to no one while the earth still stands secure — or rather, sealed shut. The kingdoms of heaven will be unlocked only when the world's transaction is complete (Rev 6:12-14). Others may claim our rest lies in the ether with Plato's disciples, or in the air with Arius, or around the moon with the Stoics' Endymions; 'No,' you say, 'it is in paradise, to which the Patriarchs and Prophets, appendages of the Lord's resurrection, have already migrated from the underworld.'

But how did John, in the Spirit, see the region of paradise subject to the altar reveal no souls there except the martyrs' (Rev 6:9)? How did Perpetua, that bravest martyr, on the day of her passion, see only her fellow martyrs in her vision of paradise — unless paradise's doorkeeper admits no one except those who have died in Christ, not in Adam? A new death for God, an extraordinary death for Christ, receives a different, private hospitality. Recognize the difference between the pagan and the faithful in death. If you die for God, as the Paraclete urges (John 16:13), not in soft fevers and sickbeds but in martyrdoms; if you take up your cross and follow the Lord as he himself commanded (Matt 16:24); then all paradise is yours, and your blood is the key. You also have from us a booklet on Paradise in which we establish that every soul is held under guard among the dead until the Day of the Lord (1 Pet 3:19; Rev 20:13).

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass B provides necessary scriptural identifications for the allusions in the Latin (e.g., Matt 12:40 for 'Christum... triduum mortis... expunctum', Luke 16:22 for 'Abrahae sinu', etc.), which is required by the instructions. Pass A maintains the clause structure and meaning of the Latin. All theological nuances regarding the distinction between the pagan and the faithful in death are preserved.
